title: How does Flink checkpointing work via barrier snapshots (barriers injected at sources flow through the graph, barrier alignment waits for a barrier on all inputs, then each task snapshots its state asynchronously to durable storage like S3/HDFS)?
shortTitle: How does Flink checkpointing work via barrier snapshots

s1_definition.oneliner: Checkpoint barriers flow from sources through the dataflow graph, each operator aligns barriers across its inputs then snapshots its state asynchronously to durable storage, producing one globally consistent recovery point.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Chandy-Lamport algorithm** – Flink checkpointing is based on this distributed snapshot algorithm that captures a consistent cut of the dataflow without stopping processing.
- **Checkpoint barriers** – Special markers injected at sources that flow downstream through the graph alongside normal records, carrying a checkpoint ID.
- **Barrier alignment** – Multi-input operators wait until the barrier arrives on all input channels before snapshotting, ensuring the snapshot is consistent.
- **Asynchronous snapshots** – State is captured and uploaded to durable storage (S3/HDFS) in the background, so the processing thread is barely blocked.
- **Coordinator acknowledgment** – When all operators acknowledge their snapshots, the checkpoint is marked complete and usable for recovery.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India wants a perfectly consistent photograph of its entire assembly line of clerks at one logical instant, without stopping the line. The checkpoint coordinator sends a special colored slip (barrier) down each conveyor. Each clerk keeps processing normal slips until the colored slip arrives. A clerk fed by two conveyors waits until the colored slip has arrived on both before taking a photo of their passbook state. Once every clerk has filed their photo, the bank has one coherent snapshot.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Flink Checkpoint Barrier Flow

  ┌──────────┐
  │ JobMgr   │ Trigger checkpoint 42
  │Coordinator│
  └────┬─────┘
       │ inject barrier(42)
       ▼
  ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐
  │ Source 1 │     │ Source 2 │
  │ B42 ──▶  │     │ B42 ──▶  │
  └────┬─────┘     └────┬─────┘
       │                │
       ▼                ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────┐
  │  Join Operator (2 inputs)  │
  │                            │
  │  Input 1: ─[R1][B42]──▶   │
  │  Input 2: ─[C1][C2]──▶    │ ◀─ B42 not yet on Input 2
  │           buffer Input 1    │    keep processing Input 2
  │                            │
  │  Input 2: ─[C3][B42]──▶   │ ◀─ B42 arrives on both
  │           SNAPSHOT state    │
  │           forward B42       │
  └────────────┬───────────────┘
               │
               ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │  Async Upload    │
  │  State → S3/HDFS │
  │  ACK → Coord     │
  └──────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Flink checkpointing is a distributed snapshot mechanism based on the Chandy-Lamport algorithm. The checkpoint coordinator in the JobManager periodically triggers a checkpoint by telling every source to inject a barrier marker into its output stream. The barrier flows downstream through the dataflow graph alongside normal records, never overtaking them, separating pre-checkpoint from post-checkpoint records.

The subtle part is barrier alignment for multi-input operators. When the barrier arrives on one input, the operator stops consuming that input and buffers its records while continuing the other inputs until their barriers arrive. Only when all barriers are present does the operator snapshot, guaranteeing the snapshot contains exactly all pre-barrier records. The snapshot is uploaded asynchronously to durable storage like S3, so the processing thread is barely blocked.

On failure, Flink restores every operator from the last completed checkpoint and rewinds sources to the stored offsets, resuming from a consistent point with exactly-once state semantics. Exactly-once end-to-end additionally requires transactional or idempotent sinks.

At the National Bank of India checkpointing was the backbone of the stateful running-balance job. Every ten seconds the coordinator triggered a checkpoint, barriers flowed through the merged retail and corporate streams, and each operator's per-account balance was snapshotted to S3. A task manager crash restored all state to one coherent instant, never losing or double-applying a transaction.

Remember one sentence: Barriers flow from sources through the graph, multi-input operators align on all barriers before snapshotting, and the async snapshot to durable storage produces one globally consistent recovery point for exactly-once state semantics.

---

keyPoints: The checkpoint coordinator injects barrier markers at sources that flow downstream alongside records, separating pre-checkpoint from post-checkpoint data.
Barrier alignment ensures multi-input operators snapshot only after receiving the barrier on all inputs, guaranteeing a consistent cut.
Snapshots are uploaded asynchronously to durable storage (S3/HDFS) so the processing thread is barely blocked.
On failure, Flink restores all operator state from the last completed checkpoint and rewinds sources to stored offsets.
Exactly-once state is guaranteed by checkpointing; end-to-end exactly-once additionally requires transactional or idempotent sinks.
Barrier alignment can amplify backpressure when one input is slow, which motivated unaligned checkpoints in Flink 1.11+.
